raw_case_text: Case 3: A 21 year old patient that reported fever in the second trimester of pregnancy. Her IgM serology for ZIKV was positive and non-reactive for dengue, chikungunya, rubella, toxoplasmosis, HIV, syphilis and cytomegalovirus. The PRNT90% was positive for neutralizing antibodies. Her IgG serology was positive for cytomegalovirus and rubella. At 41 weeks of gestation, her baby girl was born by cesarean delivery that presented a cephalic circumference of 36 cm.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 21-year-old pregnant woman presented with acute fever during the second trimester of pregnancy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The 21-year-old patient developed a febrile illness during the second trimester of gestation and was monitored through term delivery at 41 weeks of gestation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Pregnant woman in the second trimester; positive maternal IgG serology for cytomegalovirus and rubella consistent with prior immunity.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever during the second trimester of pregnancy.

objective.physical_examination: At 41 weeks of gestation, her female newborn delivered via cesarean section had a head (cephalic) circumference of 36 cm.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Confirmed maternal Zika virus infection in the second trimester of pregnancy with delivery of a normocephalic female infant at 41 weeks of gestation. Maternal ZIKV infection was confirmed by positive ZIKV IgM serology and positive 90% plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT90%) for neutralizing antibodies. Maternal IgM serologies were non-reactive for dengue, chikungunya, rubella, toxoplasmosis, HIV, syphilis, and cytomegalovirus (with reactive IgG for cytomegalovirus and rubella). She delivered a healthy baby girl by cesarean section at 41 weeks of gestation (head circumference 36 cm).
